A collection about internet culture needs room for more than its most familiar symbols. This display puts shared characters and public statements alongside landscape, photography and works that complicate the idea of an individual author.
The accompanying notes explain why each work entered the collection. The three groupings offer different routes through it; the acquisition register records how those choices were made.

A public online display, with a collection session on 26 September and a complete work checklist.

items.title: Don't Trust, Check. by Jack Butcher

blocks.content: 01 / Four works

A screenshot, an exhortation, a network and a joke about institutions. These works turn forms already circulating online into collection objects. FirstGM and Don't Trust, Check. make a useful pair: one preserves a particular statement, while the other asks how a statement earns our trust.
Selected by Amina Chen. The checklist keeps the original wording and source references with each work.
02 / Four works

Recognition travels faster than attribution. Pairing Arsonic and Tyronejkd gives us two distinct treatments of Pepe; OSF and XCOPY extend the selection beyond a single shared character. The grouping keeps those differences in view instead of treating meme art as one style.
Luca Bell's display checklist identifies the two animated originals in this group. The gallery uses still previews with links to their original media.

items.title: The Socially Umpired Animals by Botto
Tears of the Desert by Ebrahim_Elmi

blocks.content: 03 / Six works

The September accessions broaden the collection beyond direct address. ACK, Cath Simard and Grant Riven Yun introduce different kinds of constructed space; Ebrahim_Elmi's portrait makes the human subject central. Botto and MaNiC provide a starting point for the session's discussion of authorship and machines.
The acquisition note records the group's reasoning without attributing unverified intentions to the artists. All six works entered under the same member decision.
Display checklist / Edition 1.0
Fourteen credited works, including three animated originals. Each object page links to its 6529 source record; the collection register supplies the programme group and accession reference.
Public programme

Amina Chen introduces the selection; Luca Bell presents the display checklist. The session will review the lending-policy responses received by 18 September. Questions will be recorded with the October report.

pages.title: Collecting mandate
pages.description: Collect digital art concerned with internet identity, shared visual culture and the ways images are made, owned and circulated.

blocks.content: The charter / Adopted 2 February 2026
Policy owner: Noor Patel Next review: December 2026
Collect digital art concerned with internet identity, shared visual culture and the ways images are made, owned and circulated.

The collection brings together individual practices and collaborative projects. The Memes and Blitmap are its first two areas of concentration. Acquisitions should deepen those areas or make a specific, documented connection to them.
Public display, research and preservation guide the programme. Member distributions and short-term trading are outside the mandate.

A proposal identifies the exact work and edition, explains its place in the collection, and records attribution, provenance, rights and media dependencies. Terms and available funds are reviewed before a vote; approval does not authorize different works or changed terms.

Proposals remain open for at least seven days. Three eligible members form a quorum; approval requires two-thirds of votes cast. A member with a financial or personal interest discloses it and abstains. Research and coordination roles do not carry additional votes.
From proposal to accession

Research: Research Publish the work, source references and collecting rationale.
Discussion: Discussion Resolve attribution, media and custody questions. Record amendments before the vote.
Decision: Decision Record each member’s vote, conflicts and any conditions attached to approval.
Execution: Execution Two designated signers confirm the approved terms. Jo reconciles the result against the accession register.

blocks.title: Custody and continuity Two-signature approval · quarterly reconciliation
blocks.content:
The collection uses a dedicated Safe. Two designated signers authorize custody transactions; one member cannot move a work alone. Signer changes require a separate member resolution.

Jo maintains the custody register and prepares quarterly reconciliation. Luca retains original media, metadata and source references independently of the website. An NFT record, a media backup and permission to exhibit are documented separately.

blocks.title: Loans and public access CIP–10 · policy under discussion
blocks.content:
The proposed checklist records the host, dates, work, format, credit line and responsible contact. A media exhibition does not automatically require a token transfer. Each proposed loan receives its own approval.

blocks.content: The members
Each member holds one vote. Operational responsibilities remain subject to the charter and collective approval.
Collection research
Amina leads collection research and edits selection rationales, with a particular interest in the relationship between digital editions and the visual conventions of print.
Current work: October exhibition and accession reviews
Archive & rights
Luca maintains media references, credit lines and rights documentation, with responsibility for the register’s completeness and long-term usability.
Current work: source records and the lending checklist
Treasury & custody
Jo oversees transaction records, custody documentation and execution planning. She reviews proposed terms before member consideration and records how approved decisions are carried out.
Current work: September accession reconciliation
Member coordination
Noor administers proposals, agendas and voting records, and coordinates the public programme. She brings questions from open sessions to member discussion.

blocks.title: Discussion CIP–10 · 11 SEP 2026 A standard record for public loans
blocks.content:
Proposer: Luca Bell Comments close: 18 September Decision pending

Record the host, display period, work, media source, credit line and responsible contact for every public loan. Distinguish permission to display media from a transfer of the NFT. Animated works require a playback check before installation.

Member comments close on 18 September. The 26 September session will consider the revised checklist; adoption and individual loan approvals remain separate decisions.

blocks.title: Registered CIP–09 · 9 SEP 2026 Six works for Authorship & imagined worlds
blocks.content:
Discussion: 2–9 September Proposer: Amina Chen 4 yes · 0 no Registered: 10 September

Approve the proposed secondary acquisitions of works by ACK, Botto, Cath Simard, Ebrahim_Elmi, Grant Riven Yun and MaNiC. The group broadens the programme beyond shared characters and public statements, and completes the October exhibition selection.

Amina, Luca, Jo and Noor voted yes. No conflicts were declared. Jo recorded completion against references CC.26.012–017; Luca’s original-format review remains a display requirement.
